body:
This is kind of a "our problem only" problem, but IMO worth considering.

See https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28129#discussion_r3905022410 for context.

TL;DR we have `uv workspace list --scripts`, which lists the paths of all PEP 723 scripts in the workspace. However, it currently bombs out if any script has an invalid PEP 723 stanza state:

```
warning: The `--scripts` option is experimental and may change without warning. Pass `--preview-features workspace-list-scripts` to disable this warning.
error: Failed to discover PEP 723 scripts under workspace root `/prefix/astral-sh/ruff`
  Caused by: Failed to parse PEP 723 script: /prefix/astral-sh/ruff/crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/eradicate/ERA001.py
  Caused by: The script contains multiple PEP 723 metadata blocks
```

(This is in Ruff's workspace, and it happens because Ruff intentionally includes invalid PEP 723 scripts as part of its test fixtures.)

A few options, probably not exhaustive:

- Maybe `uv workspace list --scripts` should warn-and-skip instead of failing hard in this case?
- Maybe we should have some kind of `--skip-invalid` option? That feels like a kludge to me though.

CC @AlexWaygood @zanieb
title: Should `uv workspace list --scripts` be resilient to malformed scripts?
